device.name: Truma iNet X / iNet X Pro Panel (strict read-only)
device.notes:
The panel is a local BLE gateway to vehicle appliances. This spec is deliberately limited to topology and conditional telemetry. Heating, cooling, hot water, fans, pumps, switches, timers, fault resets, configuration, firmware and bond management are outside its scope. identify_only remains until a consumer implements the CBOR/control transport and the reduced read sequence passes an owner-panel test.
READ-ONLY STILL WRITES GATT: control and request characteristics must be written to announce and issue reads. The general community client's normal discovery also emits client-system-time and client-last-message frames; those change client state and are NOT passive. Omit both from a strict-read client. Do not send {tn,pn,v} setters, measurement triggers, install/demo operations or pairing/bond APIs.
DO NOT MIX PROTOCOLS: the legacy iNet Box uses ASCII TRBT: frames over Nordic UART, specified separately in truma-inet-box.yaml. Never send TRBT to an iNet X panel or these CBOR envelopes to an iNet Box.
IDENTITY: the advertised name prefix is Truma iNetX, possibly delivered in a scan response, and advertised service fc310001-…. Community evidence reports a rapidly rotating resolvable private address. Do not persist MAC, weaken host privacy or clear bonds to make telemetry work. Pairing is reported Just Works only in the panel's add-device mode with about four bond slots.
TELEMETRY MODEL: retain (source group, topic, parameter) with every value. Group hints are not universal: heating often uses 0x0201, tanks/switches 0x0405, room climate 0x0101, while one air conditioner appeared at 0x0406. Discover Devices and each response's actual source. Device-supplied availability/permission metadata is not proof that hardware is absent or permission to actuate. Refresh ranges and enums per vehicle.

enter_pairing_mode.notes: About four bond slots are reported; no pairing window duration is asserted.

procedures.basis: Community pairing documentation reports that bonding is accepted only in add-device mode; exact panel-menu steps were not verified.
procedures.name: Panel add-device mode

steps.action: Open add-device mode on the panel and keep the panel nearby.
steps.expect: The panel accepts a Just Works bond while a slot is available.

exclusivity.notes: Approximately four bond slots, not one. Host-specific Linux/ESPHome reports are not blanket claims that an adapter cannot work.
exclusivity.recovery: Close the other client and retry with an existing bond or a free add-device slot; do not clear all bonds or change adapter privacy.

pairing.notes: Just Works has no MITM protection. Bonding is required by the reported client flow but was not tested by this project.

unpair.notes: No bond-management route is included in this strict-read spec.

credentials.notes: The assigned address is session routing state, not an appliance-control credential. Redact identity and account fields from diagnostics.

factory_reset.effect: No factory-reset or bond-clear procedure is established or recommended for telemetry. Do not erase an owner's panel to make a client connect.

methods.basis: Community pairing/connectivity reports and the MIT transport implementation; not replayed on a panel.

ble.pin_source: None — reported Just Works; no passkey.

methods.description: Use the panel's add-device mode, bond with Just Works, subscribe to control/data, then retain the client address returned by the protocol- version exchange. Do not clear existing bonds or send time updates.
methods.name: Add-device bonding and strict-read onboarding

steps.action: Open the panel's add-device mode using its own UI; the exact menu path is not asserted here.
steps.expect: The panel accepts a new Just Works bond while a slot is available.

steps.action: Scan by name or advertised service, connect and complete Just Works bonding without changing host privacy settings.
Subscribe to control and data notifications and run only protocol_details.strict_read.sequence; omit clock/last-message frames and all setters.
steps.expect: Protocol version and an assigned client address are returned; stop if the response or framing differs.

setup.notes: Bonding is required by the reported community flow. No clock or last-message update is part of this setup route. The reduced read-only sequence itself remains unverified on hardware.

rejoin.notes: Reuse the existing bond and rediscover by name/service rather than MAC. A new client needs the add-device flow and a free slot; do not factory reset merely because the address changed.

testing.notes: No panel, appliance, account, adapter or credential was used by this project. Facts derive from the MIT Node/TypeScript client at 004a8327, independent Home Assistant behavior at 08daf61c, vendor documents and static app analysis. Upstream build/lint/70 tests and nine synthetic transport checks passed, but the reduced strict-read sequence has not been run on a bonded owner panel.

image.format: Unknown; panel firmware is supplied through the vendor app

dfu.notes: Vendor documentation says the app is required for panel firmware updates. No update transport or image format was researched, and this strict-read spec deliberately provides no update operation.

initialization.notes: Control notifications drive the request/response state machine.
Reassemble data to each control-announced length; responses may be queued.

covers: Topic registration, device-list and per-group read requests
Length-driven response reassembly and source-group-aware telemetry
Conditional temperature, tank, voltage, shore-power, fan and active-state readings
not_covered: All appliance settings/actions, measurement triggers, timers, fault resets and install/demo operations
Clock/last-message updates, firmware, pairing management and remote-module configuration
local_access.summary: A bonded client can perform local topology and telemetry reads using a framed CBOR request/response exchange. No appliance actuation is declared.

control_exchange.fragmentation_warning: A short first fragment can be mistaken for trailing data after a completed response. Use announced lengths and explicit frame state, then test real ATT/MTU splits.
steps: Wait for 81 00, then write the complete request on request.
Reassemble data notifications to the announced length; allow queued responses and a new frame while old responses drain.
Acknowledge each flushed response with f0 01.

cbor.presence: normal frames when a body is present

frame.group_read_template: 000000050b00030000000000000000000400; replace target at 0 and learned source at 2, little-endian
frame.integer_endianness: little for all multi-byte header fields; CBOR has its own encoding
frame.validation: Check complete physical length and header before trying CBOR; a CBOR decoder's offset search is not frame validation.

strict_read.completeness_unknown: Whether omitting clock/last-message frames changes availability or complete telemetry needs an owner-panel test.

sequence.name: protocol_version
sequence.result: pv and assigned client addr; retain addr as source for the session

sequence.body: Send the four concrete CBOR batches in strict_read.topic_registration.batches in order
sequence.name: topic_registration

sequence.body: Substitute the learned source into device_list source_lo/source_hi; 18-byte header without CBOR
sequence.name: device_list

sequence.body: Replace target and learned source in group_read_template
sequence.name: group_read

topic_registration.cbor_encoding: Definite-length map {tn: array}; tn is a text key and every array entry is an exact-case UTF-8 topic text string

max_topics_per_request.basis: Observed batches and independent protocol references; not independently boundary-tested

selection.broad_discovery: Send all four batches in the listed order before device_list; Devices supplies source group IDs, not topic names
selection.empty_array: Not a wildcard or all-topics request; no wildcard semantics are established
selection.group_routing: Discover group targets with device_list; topic names do not determine group routing
selection.selected_reads: Use nonempty exact-case subsets needed for telemetry, preserve their order, and split them into sequential requests of at most ten names

topic_registration.source: The addr assigned by the protocol-version response, little-endian at frame offset 2

synthetic_frame.source_note: Invented assigned client address 0x1234 for this vector

active.caveat: Do not apply to RoomClimate.Active type 107.

heating_activity.caveat: Follows gas or electric heat, not only a flame.
heating_activity.name: System.FlameStatus

tanks.caveat: Conditional on the installed vehicle and stale until a new measurement is requested; trigger writes are excluded.

temperatures.caveat: One Victron example uses tenths of a degree C and rejects 65535; neither is universal.

unresolved.caveat: Remaining-time interpretation was not substantiated; keep raw/unitless.
unresolved.name: GasBtl.RemTime

voltage.caveat: Retain the electrical block's source group.

telemetry.privacy: Redact CertThumb, Muid, SerialNr, UniqueID, UserName, Uuid, real MACs, assigned labels, raw identity responses and account data by default.

remaining_unknowns: Live pairing/encryption, Panel 1/Panel 2 inventory, strict-read completeness, real ATT/MTU fragmentation and firmware compatibility.
Per-parameter scales/sentinels, optional remote-module behavior and whether any read requires the omitted clock/last-message frames.
Factory reset, standalone unpairing, update transport and recovery. None should be probed with appliance writes.

acknowledge_response.description: Acknowledge each flushed response; also wait for f0 01 after sending a request.

announce_request.description: Announce the complete outgoing request length before writing it.

length_hi.description: High byte of the complete physical request length.

length_lo.description: Low byte of the complete physical request length.

request_response.description: After control 83 <length_lo> <length_hi>, request the waiting response.

characteristics.name: Control
characteristics.notes: Wait for 81 00 before writing the request. Transport acceptance is not proof of a setting change.

device_list.description: Request source groups; replace the learned source in the template before use. A reply may be [0, {Devices: [group, ...]}].

source_hi.description: High byte of the assigned client source.

source_lo.description: Low byte of the assigned client source.

group_read_template.description: Operation-3 group read with flags 0x0004; replace target and learned source before use.

source_hi.description: High byte of the assigned client source.

source_lo.description: Low byte of the assigned client source.

target_hi.description: High byte of the discovered target group.

target_lo.description: Low byte of the discovered target group.

protocol_version.description: Request protocol version and an assigned client address; retain that source address for this session.

characteristics.name: Request
characteristics.notes: These are read envelopes only. Build registrations from strict_read.topic_registration: four concrete CBOR {tn: [...]} batches with target zero, the learned source, operation 3 and flags 0x0002.

characteristics.name: Data
characteristics.notes: Validate physical/header lengths before CBOR. Do not rely only on the upstream short-trailing-fragment heuristic.

characteristics.name: Optional Additional Notification
characteristics.notes: Optional in the MIT client; control, request and data are required.

characteristics.name: Software Revision
characteristics.notes: UTF-8 software revision string; variable length, so no fixed-width format is declared.
